classification.difficultyReason: Preserve the shaded proportion across prepartitioned circles and fill missing numerators, including recognising two eighths as one quarter before shading other models.

content.prompt: Produce equivalent fractions by shading these circles.

spec.description: Three equally sized circles in a horizontal row, divided into 2, 4 and 6 equal sectors. Only the right half of the first circle is shaded.
spec.mathematics: One half is equivalent to two quarters and three sixths.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied half remains visible; the quarters and sixths remain unshaded.

answer.short: $\frac{1}{2}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{3}{6}$. Shade 2 of the 4 sectors and 3 of the 6 sectors.
answer.worked:
Splitting each half into two equal parts gives four equal parts altogether, with two shaded. Splitting each half into three equal parts gives six equal parts altogether, with three shaded.
$$\frac{1}{2}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{3}{6}$$

spec.description: Completed equal-sized circle models with 1 of 2, 2 of 4 and 3 of 6 sectors shaded.
spec.mathematics: All three shaded regions occupy half of the same-sized whole.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete solution shading appears only in answers.

spec.description: Three equally sized circles in a horizontal row, divided into 3, 6 and 9 equal sectors. The right and lower thirds of the first circle are shaded.
spec.mathematics: Two thirds is equivalent to four sixths and six ninths.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied two thirds remains visible; the sixths and ninths remain unshaded.

answer.short: $\frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{6}=\frac{6}{9}$. Shade 4 of the 6 sectors and 6 of the 9 sectors.
answer.worked:
Splitting each third into two equal parts gives six equal parts altogether, with four shaded. Splitting each third into three equal parts gives nine equal parts altogether, with six shaded.
$$\frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{6}=\frac{6}{9}$$

spec.description: Three equally sized circles in a horizontal row, divided into 5, 10 and 15 equal sectors. Two adjacent sectors on the right of the first circle are shaded.
spec.mathematics: Two fifths is equivalent to four tenths and six fifteenths.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied two fifths remains visible; the tenths and fifteenths remain unshaded.

answer.short: $\frac{2}{5}=\frac{4}{10}=\frac{6}{15}$. Shade 4 of the 10 sectors and 6 of the 15 sectors.
answer.worked:
Splitting each fifth into two equal parts gives ten equal parts altogether, with four shaded. Splitting each fifth into three equal parts gives fifteen equal parts altogether, with six shaded.
$$\frac{2}{5}=\frac{4}{10}=\frac{6}{15}$$

spec.description: Three equally sized circles in a horizontal row, divided into 4, 8 and 12 equal sectors. Only the two upper-right sectors of the middle circle are shaded.
spec.mathematics: Two eighths is equivalent to one quarter and three twelfths.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied two eighths remains visible; the quarters and twelfths remain unshaded.

answer.short: $\frac{1}{4}=\frac{2}{8}=\frac{3}{12}$. Shade 1 of the 4 sectors and 3 of the 12 sectors.
answer.worked:
The two shaded eighths together occupy one quarter of the circle. Splitting each quarter into three equal parts gives twelve equal parts altogether, with three shaded.
$$\frac{1}{4}=\frac{2}{8}=\frac{3}{12}$$
